chunks.heading: A 9-5 Could Kill You
chunks.notes: Introduces an isolated, self-loathing protagonist whose toxic post-breakup worldview and medication non-compliance spiral into quitting his job and bed-rotting.

chunks.heading: A 9-5 Could Kill You
chunks.notes: Reality destabilizes as the protagonist hallucinates a normal life and begins talking to, then dating, his own mirror reflection personified as a separate person.

chunks.heading: Part Three — Hate Rears Its Ugly Head
chunks.notes: The personified partner is "killed," triggering rampaging grief episodes that end with the protagonist setting his own house on fire and being arrested.

chunks.heading: Part Four — Time with His Therapist
chunks.notes: In therapy the protagonist mourns the personified "partner" and admits he loved that toxic version of himself, marking the first emotional break in his denial.

chunks.heading: Part Five — Living After It All
chunks.notes: A quiet, unglamorous recovery closes with a callback to the mirror motif -- he glimpses the "partner" in a reflection and simply nods and walks on.
